column1: # RHJ BATCH-SIZE LADDER -- the PUBLISHED arm (Y06) at batch 512 / 256 / 128 / 64 / 32
# OBJECTIVE. Best model on UNSEEN perturbations in HepG2 from one control cell (RHJ few-shot,
# split-half paired protocol, 5 splits, cell-eval 0.6.0, nocal). Headline: pearson_delta.
# Anchors: ctrlcell -0.0018 · ctrlmean 0.0016 · meanpert 0.1324 · transfer 0.2323 ·
# QUESTION. Norman improved monotonically as batch size fell (NE25 bs128 beat bs2048 on pd and
# mae, F-sweep1). Norman had 27 steps/epoch at bs 2048; RHJ has 298. Does smaller batch also
# help on RHJ, where optimisation is NOT step-starved?
# VARIED: batch_size only. HELD FIXED: every other Y06 setting -- Q02 loss (smooth_l1, dcos 0.5,
# mag 0.01363, lmse 0.0044, delta_z), 150 epochs, eta_min 3e-4, lr 1e-3 (NOT rescaled with
# batch), seed 42. Same checkpoint selection as Y06 (RHJ validation metric).
# WHAT EACH OUTCOME MEANS
#   smaller batch beats Y06 on the 4 headline metrics -> the gain is a gradient-noise /
#     step-count effect that generalises beyond Norman; bs becomes a live RHJ knob.
#   flat or worse -> the Norman gain was step starvation (27 steps/epoch), not a general
#     property; RHJ stays at 2048.
# ⚠️ lr is held at 1e-3 across the ladder, so batch and effective lr/step-noise co-vary.
# WALLTIME: Y06 took 2h06m at bs 2048. Steps grow 4x..64x; launched with 24h..72h.
